confidence_notes: I estimated the food and coffee anchors by triangulating several aggregated cost-of-living sites. Those sites cite Numbeo, Expatistan, CityCost and similar sources, and they disagree by quite a lot, so I used middle values. I converted rupees to USD at about INR 88-92 per USD, from general knowledge. The inexpensive meal (about INR 300-330) and cappuccino (about INR 100-150) are fairly well supported. For the mid-range meal for two, aggregated figures range from about INR 850 to 1,200 or more. Q1 2026 data put it near USD 18, so I chose about INR 1,350. For beer, sources give about INR 160 for a domestic draught pint and about INR 246 for a pub beer. I set the restaurant serving higher, because licensed restaurant and bar prices in Jaipur include state excise and taxes. The cocktail is based on Expatistan's INR 717 club figure, which comes from only 8 data points and is dated 2023, and on its usual ratio to beer. The wine glass sits below the hotel-bar prices found (about INR 950-1,500 for Indian or imported wine at a Hyatt). It reflects Indian wine such as Sula or Grover at standalone licensed restaurants, so it is uncertain. The accommodation anchors come only from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. I assumed July pricing, which is the hot, monsoon low season in Rajasthan, so these numbers may understate the October-March peak. The RBA rate is the latest observation available on the generation date (18 Nov 2026), which falls after the July 2026 pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: Jaipur is a large tier-2 Indian city and a major tourist destination. Restaurant prices are slightly below Delhi and Mumbai and similar to Udaipur and Jodhpur. Accommodation compares with other Golden Triangle cities such as Agra, where budget hostel chains like Zostel are common and there are many mid-range heritage-style 3-star hotels.
